p: and it sees what is on the ground.
Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yosi and the Chachamim:
if it were placed on the ground,
a vessel of a tefach and a half,
if it were on the ground,
כְּלִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ שָׁלֹשׁ אֶצְבָּעוֹת כוּלֵּי.
a vessel that is three fingerbreadths," etc.
Now their dispute needs to be understood.
that it sees from twenty-five mil —
that the hawk species sees from afar.
And so there is in the Gemara (Chullin 63b):
and why is it called ra'ah?
it sees carcasses that are in Eretz Yisrael.
But the dispute about the vessel —
or a tefach and a half
who knows the sight of the hawk?
כָּל מִי שֶׁמְּקַיֵּים מִצְוַת סוּכָּה כוּלֵּי
Whoever fulfills the mitzvah of sukkah, etc.,
be able to look upon it,
'A path that no bird of prey knows,
nor has the eye of the hawk seen it.'"
"A path that no bird of prey knows,"
"The path of the Tree of Life,
who flies like a bird," etc.
includes all ten middos of the kelipah.
And ayah — it is brought from the holy Arizal
(עֵץ חַיִּים, שַׁעַר מִעוּט הַיָּרֵחַ פֶּרֶק ג)
And correspondingly, one opposite the other,
there is in the kelipah too an ayah,
which includes the first three of the kelipah,
who was the daas of the kelipah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קצד, א),
and daas includes all the first three,
and so too in the kelipah.
And Amalek is "the first of the nations,"
and Amalek and Bilam are one,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קצד, א).
And this is the matter of their dispute about a vessel:
the body is called a vessel,
as we find in the Gemara (Taanis 7a):
And so said our holy Rebbe,
זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
may the memory of the holy tzaddik be for a blessing for life in the World to Come,
"Purify yourselves, bearers of the vessels of Hashem":
the souls of Yisrael were refined
And so it is written in the holy Zohar
that the bodies and souls of Yisrael
are called the vessels of Hashem.
that even a vessel of three tefachim —
And this is according to what is said
"And he raises it a tefach from the ground,"
in the secret of the yud;
and the first three are three tefachim.
And he said that a soul that merits
for the kelipah of the hawk can
bring in the kelipah through sight,
like Bilam, of whom it is written
"And he saw from there the edge of the people."
a vessel of a tefach and a half,
that the yud together with the upper tip,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג י, ב),
and the first three are a tefach and a half.
a vessel that is three fingerbreadths.
This is according to what is brought:
alef-tzadi equals in gematria the names Havayah and Adnus;
Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah
refers to a soul that is comprised
Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah
that is, that over them will shelter
so that the kelipah cannot enter.
And about this it is said,
"A path that no bird of prey knows" —
referring to Samael, as the Targum renders it,
that he will not be able to enter
And this is what is said,
nor has the eye of the hawk seen it":
this is the daas of the kelipah,
the power of Bilam, which was in sight —
he will not be able to see
and harm them with his gaze
And this is the sukkah of Sedom;
and one merits a portion of it
so that the bird cannot look upon it.
